summary:
ARES-1 is an interactive 10-Sol Mars outpost survival and systems-engineering simulator designed for young learners aged 7–12. In many STEM games, space missions are reduced to simple arcade clicks, while real spacecraft documentation is too technical for elementary students. ARES-1 bridges that gap by turning real Martian environmental trade-offs into hands-on engineering choices.

Cadets choose between three Martian landing sites mapped with NASA Mars Trek tiles (Jezero Crater, Arcadia Planitia, and Olympus Mons), allocate a finite 9-unit electrical power grid across life support, CSA-inspired hydroponics, radiation shielding, and communications, and respond to daily space-weather and habitat alerts driven by live NASA DONKI, NOAA GOES-18, NASA OSDR, and NASA RadLab data. Each decision records exact vitals changes in an inspectable Flight Recorder Log alongside plain-language science notes, helping kids understand how astronauts balance survival systems on Mars.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

ARES-1 puts junior astronauts (ages 7–12) in charge of keeping a Martian research habitat running for 10 Sols:

1. Landing Site Trade-Offs (NASA Mars Trek): Players choose between Jezero Crater Delta (LZ-01), Arcadia Planitia Ice Sheet (LZ-02), and Olympus Mons Foothills (LZ-03). Each zone renders Viking 232m mosaic tiles and modifies starting solar flux, subsurface water-ice reserves, and cosmic radiation exposure.

2. Tactile Power Bus Management (GRID CAP): Cadets distribute 9 daily power units (dropping to 7 during uncleaned dust storms) across four subsystems—O2 Scrubber, CSA Bio-Dome, RadLab Shield, and Comms & Array. Assigning 2 bars maintains break-even, under 8 total bars recharges the battery bank, and 9 bars draws down reserves, with live projected per-Sol deltas shown before advancing.

3. Crisis Events & Flight Recorder Log: Over 10 Sols, players resolve solar flares, dust storms, hydroponic failures, and radiation spikes informed by short NASA/CSA science notes. Every event and resource delta is saved in a clickable Flight Recorder Log and ends with a Cadet Mission Report and JPL Mars postcard.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Turns abstract aerospace concepts (power budgets, radiation dosimetry, closed-loop water recycling) into intuitive visual feedback through a dynamic animated outpost viewport (moving solar arc, growing crops, patrolling rover, storm effects, and warning beacons).

- Includes instant English / Chinese language switching and synthesized Web Audio API feedback for broader accessibility in classrooms and workshops.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide icons, and custom Web Audio API sound synthesis (zero external backend database required).

- Live Feed Resilience & CORS Proxy: Live API data caches in sessionStorage with verified archival fallbacks so classroom and judging demos run smoothly even offline. Lightweight proxy endpoints (/api/osdr and /api/radlab) handle CORS in both Vite dev mode and the Electron server.

- Desktop Distribution (v1.0.0): Packaged with Electron 45 and electron-builder into standalone executables for Windows (portable .exe and .zip), macOS (Apple Silicon arm64 and Intel x64 .zip), and Linux (.AppImage and .tar.gz), available at: https://github.com/BoyuLi0422/nasa-spaceapps-ares1-trainer/releases/tag/v1.0.0

Super Intelligence (SI) Transparency Note

An AI coding assistant was used during development to help scaffold TypeScript/React components, refine bilingual UI text, and configure Electron desktop packaging scripts. All live space-agency data feeds, UI design direction, and game rules were verified and tested directly by the team.
